Power Spikes: Know When You're Strong

Every champion has moments where they suddenly get much stronger. Learn the level, item and objective spikes, and how to fight on yours and avoid the enemy's.

What a power spike is

A power spike is a moment where your champion gets noticeably stronger in a short time. It can be a new level, a finished item, an ultimate coming off cooldown, or a buff from an objective. The whole game is a series of spikes for both teams.

Good players aren't always mechanically better. They just fight when they're on a spike and the enemy isn't, and back off when it's the other way around. If you only learn one advanced habit, learn this one: before every fight, ask "who just got stronger?"

Level spikes

Levels matter most in the first part of the game, because each new level unlocks or upgrades an ability.

LevelWhy it matters
2Your second ability. In bot lane, the team that reaches level 2 first can often force a big trade or kill. It takes the first wave plus three minions of the second.
3Your full basic kit. Most junglers gank around level 3, and many champions can all-in now.
6Your ultimate. This is the biggest early spike. Champions like Malphite, Veigar and Annie become a kill threat the moment they hit 6.
11 and 16Ultimate rank 2 and 3: more damage and a shorter cooldown.

Watch the enemy's level, not just yours. If your lane opponent gets the last minion of a wave and hits 6 a few seconds before you, they have a window where they can fight with their ultimate and you can't. Step back until you level up too.

Top laners now get a level cap of 20 from their role quest, so a top laner who finishes their quest keeps gaining stats after everyone else maxes out.

Common mistakeFighting just before your opponent levels up, without noticing. Look at their experience bar (click on them) when a wave is about to die.

Item and component spikes

Your first finished item is usually the biggest item spike of the game. For many mages that's something like Luden's Echo or Malignance; for marksmen it's often Kraken Slayer or Infinity Edge.

But you don't need full items to spike. Smaller parts (components) make a real difference in lane:

  • Needlessly Large Rod or B. F. Sword is a big damage jump for one recall.
  • Sheen gives an instant burst of damage to champions who use it, like Ezreal or Jayce.
  • Tiamat lets many fighters clear waves much faster.

Two-item and three-item spikes are when champions really come online. A marksman with Infinity Edge and a second crit item does far more damage than one with one item. Count enemy items before fights: click on them, or press Tab to see the scoreboard.

Pro tipIf you recall with enough gold for a big component, buy it even if it's not your next item in order. Being stronger right now usually beats following a build guide perfectly.

Early, mid and late game champions

Every champion is strongest at a certain point:

  • Early game champions (Renekton, Draven, Lee Sin, Pantheon) hit hard right away but fall off. They need to snowball: take kills, plates and objectives early.
  • Mid game champions (Ahri, Viego, Jayce) peak around two or three items. They want to force fights from about 15 to 30 minutes.
  • Late game champions (Kayle, Kassadin, Smolder, Veigar) are weak early and become monsters later. They just need to survive and farm.

This tells you how to play the whole game. If your team is late-game and theirs is early-game, your job in the first 15 minutes is simple: don't die, don't fight unless you must, and trade objectives instead of contesting them badly. If it's the other way around, be aggressive while your window is open, because it closes.

Objective buffs are spikes too

Neutral objectives give temporary or permanent power that changes who should fight:

  • Dragons give stacking permanent buffs, and four of them give the Dragon Soul. A team one drake from Soul is about to spike.
  • Void Grubs (three at 8:00) help take turrets, which leads to more gold.
  • Baron Nashor (from 20:00) gives Hand of Baron for 180 seconds: bonus AD and AP that grow with game time, faster recalls, and much stronger minions. Use those three minutes to push, not to farm the jungle.
  • Elder Dragon gives a burn and executes enemies below 20% health for 150 seconds. Fights with Elder are almost unwinnable for the other team.

When the enemy has Baron or Elder, the right move is often to back off, defend under your turrets, and wait for the buff to run out.

Spotting the enemy's spike

Some quick habits:

  • After an enemy recalls, assume they bought something. Click them when they come back to see their items.
  • Watch for ultimates coming back. If the enemy Malphite used his ultimate 90 seconds ago, it might be ready again.
  • Count enemy levels before Dragon fights. A two-level difference is huge.
  • If a fed enemy just completed a big item, don't take an even fight for the next minute. Let them waste their timing.

Key takeaways

  • Before every fight, ask who just got stronger.
  • Level 2, 3 and 6 are the biggest early spikes; watch the enemy's experience bar.
  • First finished items and big components are strong spikes; count enemy items with Tab.
  • Early champions must snowball; late champions must survive. Play to your team's timing.
  • Baron and Elder are huge temporary spikes: push with them, and wait them out when the enemy has them.
